name: Anthropic Claude - Associate (CCAO-F)
source: Anthropic CCAO-F questions. Stems, choices, and official answer keys transcribed from ExamTopics. Only questions provided are included; missing numbers are not fabricated.

cards.q:
A learning specialist is configuring a Project for course-design work. Their organization has an internal instructional-design standard and a preferred output structure for lesson outlines.
Which custom-instruction set best supports this use case?
options: Name Claude’s role as a course designer; let each chat’s prompt specify the standards and output structure for that lesson, since lessons vary widely.
Name Claude’s role as a course designer and require alignment to the organization’s instructional-design standards; leave output structure to Claude based on the topic of each lesson.
Specify only the preferred output structure for lesson outlines, since the structure carries the standards implicitly and naming the role adds no value.
Name Claude’s role as a course designer, require alignment to the organization’s instructional-design standards, and specify the preferred output structure for lesson outlines.
cards.a: D. Name Claude’s role as a course designer, require alignment to the organization’s instructional-design standards, and specify the preferred output structure for lesson outlines.

cards.q:
You are a project manager reviewing stakeholder messages that teammates have drafted about Claude’s role in a workflow. Which two messages are appropriate for stakeholder communication about Claude? (Choose two.)
Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: a claim that the model never makes errors and requires no quality review
a vague reassurance that “the AI is taking care of it” without further detail
a claim that Claude will handle every task without any human involvement
a clear statement of the limits and known failure modes of the integration
an honest description of where Claude assists and where humans retain decisions
cards.a: D. a clear statement of the limits and known failure modes of the integration ; E. an honest description of where Claude assists and where humans retain decisions

cards.q:
You are reviewing a Claude-generated competitor brief for unsupported claims.
Which is the correct order of review steps?
(1) Cross-check each specific claim against the supplied source material or trusted external references.
(2) Decide whether to correct, re-prompt, or escalate based on findings.
(3) Document each unsupported or inconsistent claim with location and severity.
(4) Identify the specific factual claims, statistics, and citations in the brief.
(5) Read the brief end to end and flag any claims that feel surprising.

You are designing a checklist for evaluating Claude outputs and must complete the upstream steps before scoring an output. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE scoring a Claude output against the checklist? (Choose two.)
Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: Define the evaluation criteria that matter for the task at hand.
Promote the approved output into the downstream production process.
Forward unacceptable outputs to a senior reviewer for second-pass review.
Specify the threshold that distinguishes acceptable from unacceptable output.
Document the final score and the reviewer comments for the audit trail.
cards.a: A. Define the evaluation criteria that matter for the task at hand. ; D. Specify the threshold that distinguishes acceptable from unacceptable output.

cards.q:
You are a business analyst deciding which output formatting and context-window practices to recommend to teammates. Which two practices represent effective use of the context window? (Choose two.)
Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: Reuse the same context block across multiple requests to avoid rebuilding it each time.
Concatenate all source documents end-to-end with no separators between them.
Paste full email threads related to the project into context so the model has complete conversational history.
Trim irrelevant material before submitting the request to keep context focused.
Use clear section headers to separate different parts of the input material.
cards.a: D. Trim irrelevant material before submitting the request to keep context focused. ; E. Use clear section headers to separate different parts of the input material.

cards.q:
Preparing an AI-assisted work product for external delivery, a senior manager is applying the AI Fluency Framework Diligence competency.
Which step best reflects Diligence principles?
options: Deliver the work product without independent verification on the basis that AI assistance shifts accountability away from the human, even though Diligence holds the human fully accountable for the output.

Delegate accountability for the AI-assisted work product to Claude itself rather than retaining it as a human obligation, contrary to the Diligence principle that humans remain accountable for AI-assisted outputs.
Skip verification of any element on the assumption that fluent output implies accuracy, even though Diligence requires the human to verify and correct AI-assisted outputs before they are acted upon.
Identify the elements of the work product that must be independently verified or corrected before delivery, and take ownership of those verifications as a professional accountability obligation.
cards.a: D. Identify the elements of the work product that must be independently verified or corrected before delivery, and take ownership of those verifications as a professional accountability obligation.

cards.q:
You are reviewing claims about prompt iteration that colleagues have made in a recent training. Which two claims about prompt iteration are accurate? (Choose two.)
Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
options: Repeated resubmission of the same prompt is the most reliable way to improve output.
Output comparison against original criteria validates whether iteration helped.
Iteration is most productive when each change targets a specific diagnosed weakness.
Iteration should stop only after every possible alternative phrasing has been tried.
More iterations always produce a better output regardless of what was changed.
cards.a: B. Output comparison against original criteria validates whether iteration helped. ; C. Iteration is most productive when each change targets a specific diagnosed weakness.

cards.q:
A Claude associate is reviewing a Claude-drafted set of customer-segment descriptions for an internal marketing brief. One description applies a generalization about a demographic group’s purchasing behavior that does not hold for individual customers in the segment.
Which response is most appropriate?
options: Revise the description to focus on observed behaviors rather than generalizations about people, and validate the revision against actual customer data.
Remove the entire customer-segment description from the brief, since any segmentation that involves demographic characteristics is likely to introduce similar issues.
Keep the description as written for the internal brief, since internal use does not carry the same risk as external publication of demographic generalizations.
Add a disclaimer to the description, noting that the generalization may not apply to all individuals in the segment, and keep the underlying description unchanged.
cards.a: A. Revise the description to focus on observed behaviors rather than generalizations about people, and validate the revision against actual customer data.

cards.q:
You are running an optimization pass on a recurring workflow.
Which is the correct order of optimization steps?
(1) Apply targeted optimization to the bottleneck step
(2) Roll out the optimized workflow to the broader team and document the change
(3) Identify the bottleneck step using measured time per step and queue length
(4) Map the current workflow steps, owners, and decision points
(5) Pilot the change with a small group and measure the effect against the prior baseline
You are a customer-success lead running an interactive workflow where each turn must respond quickly and the per-turn reasoning is light. Which selection best aligns to the requirements?
options: Choose any model because latency does not vary by model.
Choose Haiku to keep latency low and to handle a light reasoning load efficiently at scale.
Choose Opus to maximize reasoning depth despite higher latency.
Choose a model based on the alphabetical order of its name.
cards.a: B. Choose Haiku to keep latency low and to handle a light reasoning load efficiently at scale.

cards.q:
You are a knowledge worker summarizing common prompt failure patterns for the team.
Which pattern most often produces vague or off-target output?
options: a prompt that names a topic but does not state the task, audience, or required output structure
a prompt that adds clear constraints on length and tone
a prompt that explicitly names the role, task, audience, and required output format
a prompt that includes a representative example of the desired output
cards.a: A. a prompt that names a topic but does not state the task, audience, or required output structure

cards.q:
You are an HR specialist reviewing data items proposed for inclusion in a Claude prompt. Which two data items are appropriate to include in a Claude prompt for a routine task? (Choose two.)
Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
options: a redacted job description that the model will adapt for a posting
accommodation request notes from an employee’s HR file needed to draft a role adjustment memo
employee ID numbers and hire dates for the team roster included to help Claude personalize onboarding communications
a compensation band summary that includes employee names and current salary figures for a specific team
an anonymized summary of an HR policy that the model will rephrase
cards.a: A. a redacted job description that the model will adapt for a posting ; E. an anonymized summary of an HR policy that the model will rephrase

cards.q:
You are a Claude associate assessing a proposed Claude use case before approving it for your team. Which is the correct order of assessment steps?
(1) Compare the use case against the organization’s policies and the relevant regulatory considerations.
(2) Document the assessment outcome and the rationale for traceability.
(3) Identify the audience, decision impact, and reversibility of the outputs.
(4) Decide whether the use case proceeds, requires modification, or is declined.
(5) Identify the data types involved and whether sensitive data is implicated.

The first output from Claude is partially useful but has tone and detail issues.
Which two refinement actions are most likely to produce a meaningfully better output? (Choose two.)
Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
options: Provide an example of an output that meets the desired standard.
Append the phrase “please do better” to the end of the original prompt.
Add a specific tone descriptor and a concrete audience to the prompt.
Increase the temperature setting and resubmit the unchanged prompt.
Resubmit the same prompt several times and select the best response.
cards.a: A. Provide an example of an output that meets the desired standard. ; C. Add a specific tone descriptor and a concrete audience to the prompt.

cards.q:
You are reviewing colleagues’ responses to feedback received on Claude-drafted communications. Which two feedback responses are productive? (Choose two.)
Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
options: declining to revise sections that were generated by Claude on the basis that the model’s output should be trusted as written
incorporating all feedback received, including contradictory suggestions, into the next draft simultaneously
deferring all feedback to a later revision cycle to avoid disrupting the current draft’s consistency
asking clarifying questions when feedback is ambiguous before acting on it
mapping each piece of feedback to the specific change made in the next draft
cards.a: D. asking clarifying questions when feedback is ambiguous before acting on it ; E. mapping each piece of feedback to the specific change made in the next draft

cards.q:
A project manager is defining how Claude can support requirements analysis for an upcoming engagement. Their team will conduct stakeholder interviews and review existing process documentation as part of discovery.
Which activity fits this domain?
options: Use Claude to generate a complete requirements list from the project name and a short description, since requirements for similar engagements are largely standard.
Use Claude to prioritize the requirements the team has already gathered, leaving the gathering itself to manual analyst work since prioritization is more time-consuming.
Use Claude to synthesize stakeholder inputs and existing process documentation into a structured list of requirements with traceability to each source.
Use Claude to conduct the stakeholder interviews directly, with the analyst reviewing the recordings afterward to confirm the requirements Claude extracted.
cards.a: C. Use Claude to synthesize stakeholder inputs and existing process documentation into a structured list of requirements with traceability to each source.
